# Client

`CloudWatchLogsClient` is the entry point. Create one per process (or per set of credentials), share
it between threads/tasks and close it on shutdown. Service functions hang off the client (see
[Functions](functions.md)).

<!-- @sdk-kit:keep functions — service-owned: client functions and their Amazon CloudWatch Logs behaviour; kept by "sdk-kit sync" -->

| Function | AWS operation | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| constructor / `create` / `new` | — | validates the config (`CONFIG` error); the AWS SDK client is built on the first call (region, credential chain or static keys, profile, optional assume role, endpoint override `url`) |
| `fromEnv()` | — | config from `GROW_AWS_CLOUDWATCH_LOGS_*`, the standard AWS variables and the AWS SDK default chain; a missing region → `CONFIG` |
| `sdkClient` config / `withSdkClient(sdk)` | — | wraps an existing AWS SDK CloudWatch Logs client; Grow TLS, proxy, hooks, headers and User-Agent do not apply to it, and `close()` leaves it usable |
| `health()` | `DescribeLogGroups` (limit 1) | **never throws** for an unhealthy or unreachable service, only for `CANCELLED` and `CONFIG`; probe timeout `min(requestTimeout, 5 s)`, no retries; authentication and permission failures still count as reachable (`healthy: true`, `details.auth`) |
| `ping()` | `DescribeLogGroups` (limit 1) | latency of an authenticated call; raises the mapped error (`AUTHENTICATION`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`, …) |
| `serverVersion()` | — | always `UNSUPPORTED`: AWS has no version endpoint |
| `close()` | — | idempotent; flushes the log clients created by this client, stops open live-tail sessions and releases connections |

`status` is `ok`, `unreachable` (network error) or the reason the probe failed. The service
functions are listed in [Functions](functions.md); client setup in all five languages is in
[Client setup](functions/client-setup.md).

<!-- @sdk-kit:endkeep -->

## Create, use and close

<!-- @sdk-kit:keep examples — service-owned: create/use/close examples per language; kept by "sdk-kit sync" -->

=== "TypeScript"

    ```ts
    import { CloudWatchLogsClient } from "@grow-codes/aws-cloudwatch-logs";

    const client = new CloudWatchLogsClient({ region: "eu-central-1", profile: "ops" });
    // or CloudWatchLogsClient.fromEnv(); add url: "http://127.0.0.1:5000" for the Moto emulator
    const health = await client.health();  // { healthy, status, details }
    const latencyMs = await client.ping(); // number (ms)
    await client.close();                  // safe to call twice

    // Cancellation and per-call deadline: every I/O method accepts { signal }
    const status = await client.health({ signal: AbortSignal.timeout(2_000) });
    ```

=== "Rust"

    ```rust
    use grow_aws_cloudwatch_logs::{CloudWatchLogsClient, CloudWatchLogsConfig};

    let config = CloudWatchLogsConfig::builder().region("eu-central-1").profile("ops").build()?;
    let client = CloudWatchLogsClient::new(config)?; // or CloudWatchLogsClient::from_env()?
    let health = client.health().await?;  // HealthStatus
    let latency = client.ping().await?;   // Duration
    client.close().await;                 // safe to call twice

    // Cancellation: drop the future, e.g. with a deadline
    let status = tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(2), client.health()).await;
    ```

    Without an async runtime, enable the `blocking` feature:

    ```rust
    let client = grow_aws_cloudwatch_logs::blocking::CloudWatchLogsClient::from_env()?;
    let health = client.health()?;
    ```

=== "Go"

    ```go
    client, err := cloudwatchlogs.NewClient(cloudwatchlogs.Config{
        Region:  "eu-central-1",
        Profile: "ops",
    }) // or cloudwatchlogs.NewClientFromEnv()
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    defer client.Close() // safe to call twice

    health, err := client.Health(ctx) // HealthStatus
    latency, err := client.Ping(ctx)  // time.Duration

    // Cancellation and deadlines come from ctx
    ctx2, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 2*time.Second)
    defer cancel()
    health, err = client.Health(ctx2)
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    from grow_aws_cloudwatch_logs import CancelToken, CloudWatchLogsClient, CloudWatchLogsConfig

    config = CloudWatchLogsConfig(region="eu-central-1", profile="ops")  # or CloudWatchLogsClient.from_env()
    with CloudWatchLogsClient(config) as client:
        health = client.health()    # HealthStatus
        latency_ms = client.ping()  # float (ms)

        # Cancel from another thread
        token = CancelToken()
        health = client.health(cancel=token)
    # close() ran; calling it again is safe
    ```

    `AsyncCloudWatchLogsClient` (extra `[async]`) has the same methods as coroutines
    (`await client.health()`, `await client.aclose()`, `async with`), and honours task cancellation.

=== "Java"

    ```java
    CloudWatchLogsConfig config = CloudWatchLogsConfig.builder().region("eu-central-1").profile("ops").build();
    try (CloudWatchLogsClient client = CloudWatchLogsClient.create(config)) { // or CloudWatchLogsClient.fromEnv()
      HealthStatus health = client.health();
      Duration latency = client.ping();

      // Async variants return CompletableFuture; cancel(true) cancels the request
      CompletableFuture<HealthStatus> pending = client.healthAsync();
      pending.orTimeout(2, TimeUnit.SECONDS).join();
    } // close() is idempotent
    ```

<!-- @sdk-kit:endkeep -->

## Lifecycle rules

- The client is safe for concurrent use. Reuse it: it keeps a connection pool.
- `close()` flushes queued work (for example log batches) within the configured deadline and is
  safe to call more than once. Any call on a closed client fails with `CANCELLED`
  (`"<operation>: client is closed"`).
- Each language also offers its idiomatic scope: TypeScript `try/finally`, Rust `close().await`
  (plus best-effort `Drop`), Go `defer client.Close()`, Python `with`/`async with`, Java
  try-with-resources.
